judgements.justification: B's Reviewer_PpQM rated 3 at confidence 5 on misreadings; B's chair called it 'safe to ignore', recommended acceptance 'in this instance' and never discussed tier, while A, with no detractor, got a spotlight.
Both committees received rebuttal material (A the MobileNet/DWS table, B the ADMM sweep and extra attacks), and no score rose in either committee.
B's only confidence-5 review was PpQM's misread 3, which the chair rightly discarded; no high-confidence expert rated above the others and was outweighed.
uhXk's 2021-08-30 edit in A added no recorded new objection and no known score change; no unanswered late objection entered either decision.
The rating gap is small (6.67 against 6.33 after the outlier), and B's 6s rest on more specific, correct limitations, so it reflects different assessments, not leniency.
A's reviewers judged the robustness claim weak yet A gave a spotlight, and B's chair capped nothing on an overstated claim; the tier gap does not come from this.
B's reviewers did not all settle on marginal scores: Sfha rated 7 at confidence 4, and c4Yo wrote the most detailed review in either committee and checked the method.
